title: Introduction
preview: This chapter translates the business framing and technical choices established in the previous chapters into a structured design baseline for \projectname. Its purpose is to identify what the platform must do, which constraints it must respect, who will interact with it, and how the final multi-layer architecture answers those needs. Unlike Chapter 3, which focused on tool selection, this chapter focuses on requirement formalization and on the architectural organization of the implemented solution. In practice, the design logic follows the same principles emphasized in modern data-intensive system engineering: clear separation of concerns, explicit data movement boundaries, and layered coordination between storage, compute, and access services \cite{kleppmann2017ddia,armbrust2021lakehouse}.
body: This chapter translates the business framing and technical choices established in the previous chapters into a structured design baseline for \projectname. Its purpose is to identify what the platform must do, which constraints it must respect, who will interact with it, and how the final multi-layer architecture answers those needs. Unlike Chapter 3, which focused on tool selection, this chapter focuses on requirement formalization and on the architectural organization of the implemented solution. In practice, the design logic follows the same principles emphasized in modern data-intensive system engineering: clear separation of concerns, explicit data movement boundaries, and layered coordination between storage, compute, and access services \cite{kleppmann2017ddia,armbrust2021lakehouse}.

title: Requirement Elicitation Context
preview: The requirements of \projectname{} were derived from three complementary sources: \begin{itemize} \item the business objective of creating a distributed customer-data foundation under the broader \initiative{} vision; \item the engineering need to ingest, store, process, validate, orchestrate, expose, and monitor heterogeneous customer-related datasets; \item the operational reality of a lightweight academic multi-node environment with security hardening requirements. \end{itemize} As a result, the chapter does not present abstract requirements in isolation. Each requirement is directly connected to an implemented capability of the platform and to the final distributed deployment model.

body:
At the logical level, \projectname{} is organized as a layered customer-data platform rather than as a monolithic data pipeline. This organization is aligned with lakehouse thinking, where raw persistence, structured table layers, metadata governance, and analytical access are coordinated but not collapsed into one opaque runtime block \cite{armbrust2021lakehouse}. Each layer has a precise responsibility in the end-to-end flow:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Ingestion layer:} receives and transports the raw input datasets through Kafka.
    \item \textbf{Bronze persistence layer:} stores replayable raw artifacts in HDFS.
    \item \textbf{Raw lakehouse layer:} structures the raw persisted inputs through Spark and Iceberg.
    \item \textbf{Metadata layer:} centralizes table definitions through Hive Metastore.
    \item \textbf{Analytical access layer:} exposes curated tables through Trino.
    \item \textbf{Transformation layer:} applies modeled transformations through dbt-spark.
    \item \textbf{Validation layer:} checks trust and structural integrity through Great Expectations.
    \item \textbf{Orchestration and observability layer:} coordinates and supervises the full process through Airflow, Prometheus, and Grafana.
\end{itemize}

This logical decomposition is important because it explains the system as a coordinated architecture rather than as a sequence of unrelated tools. It also clarifies why the same dataset may pass through different representations before becoming a trusted analytical asset.

title: End-to-End Data Flow
preview: The end-to-end operational flow of the platform can be summarized in the following sequence: \begin{enumerate} \item source datasets are prepared and published through the ingestion workflow; \item Kafka receives and organizes the movement through controlled topics; \item bronze artifacts are landed in HDFS as replayable raw persistence; \item Spark reads the bronze zone and loads structured raw tables into the lakehouse; \item Hive Metastore registers the table definitions; \item Trino exposes analytical access to the governed tables; \item dbt-spark applies business-oriented transformations; \item Great Expectations validates the resulting datasets; \item Airflow orchestrates and supervises the sequence; \item Prometheus and Grafana expose the monitoring evidence. \end{enumerate} \begin{figure}[H] \centering \input{90_assets/latex_diagrams/chapter_4/fig_4_3_end_to_end_flow.tex} \captio

title: Security-by-Design Integration
preview: Security is not positioned as an external afterthought. It is integrated into the design of the platform through explicit controls attached to core layers. This follows the same engineering rationale as the rest of the architecture: identity, traffic protection, and protected storage boundaries are treated as part of the system design itself, not as a late operational patch \cite{apache_hadoop_docs,mit_kerberos_docs,cryptsetup_docs}. Security is not positioned as an external afterthought. It is integrated into the design of the platform through explicit controls attached to core layers. This follows the same engineering rationale as the rest of the architecture: identity, traffic protection, and protected storage boundaries are treated as part of the system design itself, not as a late operational patch \cite{apache_hadoop_docs,mit_kerberos_docs,cryptsetup_docs}. Table~\ref{tab:chapter4-security-controls} summarizes this logic.

\begin{table}[!htbp]

title: Design Rationale and Trade-offs
preview: The final design is the result of deliberate engineering trade-offs rather than maximum-complexity choices: \begin{itemize} \item \textbf{Distributed proof over oversized scale:} the architecture demonstrates real service distribution while remaining feasible on lightweight academic VMs. \item \textbf{Layering over monolithic simplification:} the system is decomposed into clear responsibilities to strengthen maintainability and defense clarity. \item \textbf{Security hardening without architectural replacement:} the security layer reinforces the platform without changing its lakehouse logic. \item \textbf{Operational clarity over hidden automation:} explicit scripts, bundles, checks, and service roles make the deployment easier to explain and debug. \item \textbf{Future readiness over premature AI claims:} the design prepares downstream Customer 360 and AI use cases without pretending th
body:
The final design is the result of deliberate engineering trade-offs rather than maximum-complexity choices:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Distributed proof over oversized scale:} the architecture demonstrates real service distribution while remaining feasible on lightweight academic VMs.
    \item \textbf{Layering over monolithic simplification:} the system is decomposed into clear responsibilities to strengthen maintainability and defense clarity.
    \item \textbf{Security hardening without architectural replacement:} the security layer reinforces the platform without changing its lakehouse logic.
    \item \textbf{Operational clarity over hidden automation:} explicit scripts, bundles, checks, and service roles make the deployment easier to explain and debug.
    \item \textbf{Future readiness over premature AI claims:} the design prepares downstream Customer 360 and AI use cases without pretending that those intelligent modules are already fully implemented.
\end{itemize}

These trade-offs are important for the jury defense because they show that the architecture was shaped by real constraints, not by arbitrary tool accumulation.

This chapter converted the business framing and technical stack into a coherent design baseline for \projectname. It formalized the main functional and non-functional requirements, described the global logical architecture, clarified the physical multi-node deployment, summarized the end-to-end data flow, and positioned security as an integrated design concern.
